question: Recent reports indicate that the disbursement of approximately PLN 2 billion (around EUR 470 million) to Poland under the European Peace Facility, intended as reimbursement for military assistance provided to Ukraine, is currently blocked in the Council. At the same time, broader EU support for Ukraine continues to face delays.

At a time when Ukraine continues to defend its sovereignty and territorial integrity against Russia’s war of aggression, sustained, timely and predictable financial support from the European Union remains essential. This includes ensuring that Member States contributing to Ukraine’s defence are duly and swiftly reimbursed. In this context: 1.
What concrete steps is the Commission taking to facilitate the rapid disbursement of reimbursements to Member States under the European Peace Facility?
What options is the Commission considering to ensure that EU financial support for Ukraine can be delivered without undue delay, including in the absence of agreement in the Council?
What is the indicative timeline for resolving the current situation, and what contingency measures are available should the deadlock persist?
The European Union must continue to demonstrate unity, reliability and leadership in its support for Ukraine.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (29.7.2026) At the Foreign Affairs Councils in May, June and July 2026, the High Representative/VicePresident has called for a resolution of the blockage of EUR 6.6 billion dedicated to Ukraine under the European Peace Facility (EPF). All twenty-seven Member States now agree on lifting the blockage.

The EU military support for Ukraine continues to flow through bilateral donations, through tailored and demand-driven support funded by the windfall profits of immobilised Russian assets channelled through the EPF, and through the unprecedented EUR 90 billion Ukraine Support Loan agreed in December 2025, two thirds of which is expected to go towards military support.

The Ukraine Support Loan Regulation1 was adopted on 24 February 2026, together with an amendment to the Ukraine Facility Regulation2. The final piece of the package (an amendment to the Multiannual Financial Framework Regulation3 was adopted later, on 23 April 2026, with unanimity. The liquidity situation of Ukraine was not at risk due to this delay. Implementation of the Ukraine Support Loan is under way.

The first disbursement of budget support was channelled through macrofinancial assistance at the end of June 2026 in parallel with the first disbursement to support Ukraine’s defence industrial capacities. The Ukraine Support Instrument under the European Defence Industry Programme4 will help rebuild and modernise Ukraine’s Defence Technological and Industrial Base.

Ukraine’s association to the European Defence Fund will support its integration into the European Defence Technological and Industrial Base, while the BraveTechEU initiative will accelerate defence innovation to meet real operational needs and strengthen links between DefenceTech industrial bases.
